rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about those who claim God has a child specifies the gravest instance within the general warning against those deserving punishment.
rows.anchor: فالأول عام في حق كل من استحق العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an often follows a general category with a singled-out case to mark it as its greatest instance, as with Gabriel and Michael among angels and messengers.
rows.anchor: إذا ذكر قضية كلية عطف عليها بعض جزئياتها تنبيها على كونه أعظم جزئيات ذلك الكلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who ascribe a child to God include Arab pagans who call angels His daughters, Christians who call Christ His son, and Jews who call Ezra His son.
rows.anchor: أحدها : كفار العرب الذين قالوا : الملائكة بنات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ascribing offspring to God is grave unbelief with immense impossible consequences, treated elsewhere in al-An'am and Maryam.
rows.anchor: إثبات الولد لله كفر عظيم ويلزم منه محالات عظيمة قد ذكرناه في سورة الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lack of knowledge can mean either no route to knowledge or that the alleged object is intrinsically impossible to know.
rows.anchor: انتفاء العلم بالشيء قد يكون للجهل بالطريق الموصل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of proof for another god similarly shows that the claim of divine offspring has no proof.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قوله : { ومن يدع مع الله إلها ءاخر لا برهان له به }

rows.speaker: نفاة القياس
rows.claim: Opponents of analogy argue that religious claims without knowledge are invalid, including speculative analogy; al-Razi points to the fuller argument elsewhere.
rows.anchor: نفاة القياس تمسكوا بهذه الآية فقالوا : هذه الآية تدل على أن القول في الدين بغير علم باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Nor their fathers’ means none of their ancestors knew, intensifying the judgment that their claim is false.
rows.anchor: أي ولا أحد من أسلافهم ، وهذا مبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling this assertion a great word is the second way the verse refutes it.
rows.anchor: النوع الثاني : مما ذكره الله في إبطاله قوله : { كبرت كلمة تخرج من أفواههم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalimatan is read accusative as specification or nominative as subject; al-Wahidi says the accusative removes ambiguity, implies ‘a great word,’ and has a stronger, emphatic exclamatory force.
rows.anchor: قرىء : { كبرت كلمة } بالنصب على التمييز وبالرفع على الفاعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suppressed ‘word’ is their claim that God took a child; a whole poem can likewise be called a word.
rows.anchor: والمراد من هذه الكلمة ما حكاه الله تعالى عنهم في قوله : { قالوا اتخذ الله ولدا }

rows.speaker: النظام
rows.claim: Al-Nazzam argues that speech is a body because the verse says the word exits mouths, exit is motion, and motion occurs only in bodies.
rows.anchor: احتج النظام في إثبات قوله : أن الكلام جسم بهذه الآية قال : إنه تعالى وصف الكلمة بأنها تخرج من أفواههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ‘exit’ describes speech because breath leaving the throat causes letters to arise; it does not prove that speech is a body.
rows.anchor: الجواب أن الحروف إنما تحدث بسبب خروج النفس عن الحلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim is so irrational that its speakers seem to repeat it by imitation while their own minds recoil from it.
rows.anchor: لا يحكم به عقلهم وفكرهم البتة لكونه في غاية الفساد والبطلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lie is any report that fails to match reality, regardless of whether its speaker believes it true.
rows.anchor: عندنا أنه الخبر الذي لا يطابق المخبر عنه سواء اعتقد المخبر أنه مطابق أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some require the speaker to know a report is false for it to be a lie; al-Razi rejects this because many assert God's offspring without knowing it is false.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من قال شرط كونه كذبا أن لا يطابق المخبر عنه مع علم قائله بأنه غير مطابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse consoles the Messenger not to grieve himself over their disbelief: he was sent to warn and give good news but cannot create faith in their hearts.
rows.anchor: لا يعظم حزنك وأسفك بسبب كفرهم فإنا بعثناك منذرا ومبشرا

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Bakhʿ is a person killing himself from rage and intense grief.
rows.anchor: بخع الرجل نفسه إذا قتلها غيظا من شدة وجده بالشيء

rows.speaker: الأخفش والفراء
rows.claim: They derive bakhʿ from exertion: ‘I strained my soul for you.’
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش والفراء أصل البخع الجهد

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha described Umar as having exhausted the earth by taking the wealth of kings.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها ذكرت عمر

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i uses bakhaʿa of land weakened by repeated cultivation and of a man who wears himself down.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي : بخعت الأرض بالزراعة إذا جعلتها ضعيفة

rows.speaker: أهل التأويل
rows.claim: Exegetes gloss ‘bakhic yourself’ as killing or destroying yourself; al-Wahidi says the underlying sense is exhausting oneself to death.
rows.anchor: أهل التأويل كلهم قالوا : قاتل نفسك ومهلكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘On their tracks’ means after them; the expression comes from a person's traces remaining after death before vanishing.
rows.anchor: أي من بعدهم يقال مات فلان على أثر فلان أي بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘report’ is the Qur'an. Al-Qadi argues that calling it hadith proves it originated; al-Razi replies that the uttered words are created.
rows.anchor: المراد بالحديث القرآن . قال القاضي : وهذا يقتضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asaf is intense grief, parsed as a cognate accusative, a purpose accusative, or, per al-Zajjaj, a verbal noun functioning as a circumstantial state.
rows.anchor: الأسف المبالغة في الحزن وذكرنا الكلام فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa answers the delayed condition ‘if they do not believe,’ though it appears before the condition.
rows.anchor: الفاء في قوله : { فلعلك } جواب الشرط

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: God adorned the earth with benefits to test people through duties yet continues providing for disbelievers; likewise Muhammad should keep calling them despite grief.
rows.anchor: خلقت الأرض وزينتها وأخرجت منها أنواع المنافع والمصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported interpretations range from plants and trees to the addition of minerals, gold, and silver.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم النبات والشجر وضم بعضهم إليه الذهب والفضة والمعادن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation includes the other animals, and another takes people themselves as earth's adornment.
rows.anchor: وضم بعضهم إلى سائر الحيوانات

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some identify people themselves as the adornment of the earth.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم بل المراد الناس فهم زينة الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earthly kinds are minerals, plants, and animals, with humans the noblest animals.
rows.anchor: فليس بالأرض إلا المواليد الثلاثة وهي المعادن والنبات والحيوان

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi excludes morally responsible humans from the adornment because they are the ones being tested, while plants and animals are included as useful things.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضي : الأولى أنه لا يدخل في هذه الزينة المكلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Adornment for it’ means adornment for the earth; what beautifies the earth may be called its adornment, just as stars adorn the sky.
rows.anchor: أي للأرض ولا يمتنع أن يكون ما يحسن به الأرض زينة للأرض

rows.speaker: هشام بن الحكم
rows.claim: Hisham says God learns events only when they occur; otherwise foreknown outcomes would remove divine and human ability to act otherwise, so testing is literal.
rows.anchor: ذهب هشام بن الحكم إلى أنه تعالى لا يعلم الحوادث إلا عند دخولها في الوجود

rows.speaker: جمهور علماء الإسلام
rows.claim: The majority hold that God eternally knows every particular; testing language means treating people as an examiner would, not learning from them.
rows.anchor: جمهور علماء الإسلام فقد استبعدوا هذا القول وقالوا : إنه تعالى من الأزل إلى الأبد

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Testing means making manifest who is most obedient and constant in worship and will attain Paradise; God imposed duties so people obey, refuting the claim that some were created for Hell.
rows.anchor: يبلوهم ليبصرهم أيهم أطوع لله وأشد استمرارا على خدمته

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The purpose-connoting lām supports the Mu'tazilite claim that God's acts are directed toward ends.
rows.anchor: تدل ظاهرا على أن أفعال الله معللة بالأغراض عند المعتزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi's school rejects divine acts being caused by purposes: needing an intermediary to obtain a purpose implies incapacity, impossible for God.
rows.anchor: التعليل بالغرض إنما يصح في حق من لا يمكنه تحصيل ذلك الغرض

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Ayyuhum is nominative as the subject despite its interrogative form; the sense is to test who acts best.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : أيهم رفع بالإبتداء إلا أن لفظه لفظ الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is adorned for trial, not perpetual enjoyment; its contents will be destroyed before recompense, and other verses show the earth itself will also be transformed.
rows.anchor: لا لأجل أن يبقى الإنسان فيها متنعما أبدا لأنه يزهد فيها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda defines al-sa'id as level ground.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : الصعيد المستوي من الأرض

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines al-sa'id as a path without vegetation.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : هو الطريق الذي لا نبات فيه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra defines al-juruz as land with no vegetation, stripped bare by grazing; the root also describes a voracious woman and a destructive sword.
rows.anchor: فقال الفراء : الجرز الأرض التي لا نبات عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same barren-land expression appears in the verse about water being driven to the barren plain.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : { نسوق الماء إلى الارض الجرز }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conjoining faith and righteous deeds indicates that righteous action is distinct from faith.
rows.anchor: العمل الصالح مغاير للإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reward is due under God's promise in al-Razi's school; the Mu'tazila say the deed itself creates entitlement, which he rejects because divine blessings already require gratitude and fulfilling an obligation earns no further obligation.
rows.anchor: وعند أصحابنا ذلك الاستيجاب حصل بحكم الوعد وعند المعتزلة لذات الفعل وهو باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating inna emphasizes deeds and their recompense, as illustrated by a line about the caliph and God's gift of kingship.
rows.anchor: كرر أن تأكيدا للأعمال والجزاء عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Those’ may be the predicate of inna with the no-loss phrase parenthetical; alternatively both phrases are predicates, or ‘those’ begins an explanation of the unspecified reward.
rows.anchor: أولئك خبر إن وإنا لا نضيع اعتراض ولك أن تجعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAdn means residence, so the gardens may be gardens of residence or a proper name for the central, noblest place in Paradise.
rows.anchor: والعدن في اللغة عبارة عن الإقامة فيجوز أن يكون المعنى أولئك لهم جنات إقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ‘gardens’ may refer to the two gardens promised to one who fears his Lord, or a separate garden for each person.
rows.anchor: ولمن خاف مقام ربه جنتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rivers beneath the gardens evoke the best worldly dwellings: orchards traversed by rivers.
rows.anchor: أفضل المساكن في الدنيا البساتين التي يجري فيها الأنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God or the angels may adorn the people with gold bracelets.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أنه يحليهم الله تعالى ذلك أو تحليهم الملائكة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say each person wears three bracelets: gold, silver, and pearl, drawing on three Qur'anic descriptions.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم على كل واحد منهم ثلاثة أسورة سوار من ذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sundus is fine, thin silk and istabraq is thick silk, a Persian word said to mean thick.
rows.anchor: والأول هو الديباج الرقيق وهو الخز والثاني هو الديباج الصفيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive ‘they are adorned’ may indicate a free gift, while their active wearing of clothing may indicate what they earned through deeds.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون اللبس إشارة إلى ما استوجبوه بعملهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ara'ik are beds inside canopies; a bed by itself is not called an arikah.
rows.anchor: الأرائك جمع أريكة وهي سرير في حجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excellent reward and resting place contrast with the earlier description of Hell as an evil resting place.
rows.anchor: في مقابلة ما تقدم ذكره من قوله : { وساءت مرتفقا }

none: Qur'an text only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable answers disbelievers who boast of wealth and supporters over poor Muslims: fortunes can reverse, while true distinction lies in obedience to God.
rows.anchor: الكفار افتخروا بأموالهم وأنصارهم على فقراء المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account makes the men Israelite brothers, Bratus and Judah, who inherited 8,000 dinars; the believer gave away his half seeking heavenly property while his brother bought land, a house, a wife, servants, and estates.
rows.anchor: كانا أخوين في بني إسرائيل أحدهما كافر اسمه براطوس والآخر مؤمن اسمه يهوذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies the pair with the companion in al-Saffat who says, ‘I had a companion.’
rows.anchor: وقيل هما المذكوران في سورة الصافات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A garden is called a jannah because its trees shade and conceal what lies beneath; the root means covering.
rows.anchor: وسمى البستان جنة لاستتار ما يستتر فيها بظل الأشجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Palms encircle the gardens as angels encircle the Throne; hifaf means sides and ahifah its plural.
rows.anchor: أي وجعلنا النخل محيطا بالجنتين نظيره قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The line about glances at the sides of a couch attests to hifaf meaning sides or surrounding edges.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : له لحظات في حفافي سريره

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says circling someone takes one object, with bi adding a second; farmers also favor fruit trees around vineyards for beauty.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : حفوه إذا طافوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Crops between the gardens provide staples and fruits, occupy a broad uninterrupted tract, and yield successive benefits at different times.
rows.anchor: أن تكون تلك الأرض جامعة للأقوات والفواكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kull and kilta are singular forms emphasizing two known nouns; explicit nouns take alif in all cases, while pronouns take alif in nominative and ya in other cases, though some retain alif throughout.
rows.anchor: كلا إسم مفرد معرفة يؤكد به مذكران معرفتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Each garden gave its fruit’ follows kilta's singular grammatical form; dual agreement is also possible by meaning.
rows.anchor: حمل على اللفظ لأن كلتا لفظه لفظ مفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘It did not wrong it’ means it did not diminish it; zulm can mean a shortfall.
rows.anchor: أي لم تنقص والظلم النقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ya'qub reads the river verb lightly, the other readers double it; the light form is basic and the intensive form reflects the river's spread like many streams.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة يعقوب وفجرنا مخففة وفي قراءة الباقين وفجرنا مشددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khilal means within or between, related to the expression ‘I went between the people.’
rows.anchor: أي وسطهما وبينهما . ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asim reads thamar with both vowels open as a plural of thimar or thamrah; Abu Amr has a still m, and the other readers round both vowels.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم بفتح الثاء والميم في الموضعين وهو جمع ثمار أو ثمرة

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abu Amr says thamar means wealth and children, supported by a poem attributed to al-Harith ibn Kalda.
rows.anchor: كان أبو عمرو بن العلاء يقول : الثمر المال والولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation of al-Harith ibn Kalda's cited poem says that people acquired wealth and children, supporting Abu Amr's gloss of thamar.
rows.anchor: ولقد رأيت معاشرا … قد أثمروا مالا وولدا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the wealth accompanying the gardens as gold and silver cash.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد الذهب والفضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conversation is reciprocal speech, from the root meaning return, as in the verse about thinking one will not return.
rows.anchor: والمحاورة مراجعة الكلام من قولهم : حار إذا رجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafar means a man's clan and companions who defend him and go out with him.
rows.anchor: والنفر عشيرة الرجل وأصحابه الذين يقومون بالذب عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rich man vaunts his social standing and wealth over the believer.
rows.anchor: وحاصل الكلام أن الكافر ترفع على المؤمن بجاهه وماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular ‘his garden’ means his worldly property alone is his garden; he has no share in the promised Paradise.
rows.anchor: المراد أنه ليس له جنة ولا نصيب في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Wronging himself’ interrupts the narrative to show he misuses blessings for ingratitude and denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: كان واضعا تلك النعم في غير موضعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He combines certainty that his garden will never perish with doubt about resurrection; ‘never’ means only during his lifetime.
rows.anchor: فالأول قطعه بأن تلك الأشياء لا تهلك ولا تبيد أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Munqalaban means return or outcome and is an accusative of specification; he assumes he will receive a better destination if returned to God.
rows.anchor: أي مرجعا وعاقبة وانتصابه على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His false inference is that worldly wealth proves merit and secures posthumous reward, though prosperity is often gradual enticement and respite.
rows.anchor: ظن أنه إنما أعطاه ذلك لكونه مستحقا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi and Ibn Kathir read ‘better than them,’ referring to the two gardens; the others read ‘better than it,’ referring to the garden he entered.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن كثير خيرا منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer's question ‘Have you disbelieved?’ establishes that doubting resurrection is unbelief.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الشاك في حصول البعث كافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first argument for resurrection is that the God who created a person initially can recreate him.
rows.anchor: لما قدر على الابتداء وجب أن يقدر على الإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second argument is that God made humans for worship rather than in vain, entailing reward and punishment; rational adulthood prepares one for obligation, so abandonment would be unreasonable.
rows.anchor: لما خلقك هكذا فلم يخلقك عبثا

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Lakinna contracts from lakin anā: the hamza is dropped, its vowel moves to nūn, and the adjacent nūns assimilate; the cited poem likewise means ‘but I do not hate you.’
rows.anchor: لكنا أصله لكن أنا فحذفت الهمزة وألقيت حركتها على نون لكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In ‘He is God, my Lord,’ huwa is the pronoun of the matter and the following nominal clause is its predicate.
rows.anchor: ضمير الشأن وقوله : { الله ربى } جملة من المبتدأ والخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lakinna rebuts ‘Have you disbelieved?’: the believer means, ‘You disbelieve, but I am a monotheist.’
rows.anchor: كأنه قال لأخيه : أكفرت بالله لكني مؤمن موحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read masculine yakun because fi'ah is a collective; the other readers use feminine agreement with the word fi'ah.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي : ( ولم يكن له فئة ) بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruined man's group could not help him independently of God; God alone can aid him.
rows.anchor: ما حصلت له فئة يقدرون على نصرته من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read al-wilayah with kasra for sovereignty; other readers use fatḥa for support or guardianship, and Abu Amr calls kasra incorrect.
rows.anchor: في قراءة حمزة والكسائي بكسر الواو وفي قراءة الباقين بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Amr and al-Kisa'i read al-haqq nominative, construing ‘true guardianship belongs to God’; others read it genitive as God's adjective.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو والكسائي قوله : الحق بالرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Nafi, al-Kisa'i, and Ibn Amir round the qaf in ʿuqban; Asim and Hamza leave it still.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع والكسائي وابن عامر عقبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘There’ may refer to the crisis when God grants His allies victory over enemies and entrusts the unbelievers to them.
rows.anchor: في مثل ذلك الوقت وفي مثل ذلك المقام تكون الولاية لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, all desperate people turn to God; the unbeliever's regret is forced by the calamity of disbelief.
rows.anchor: في مثل تلك الحالة الشديدة يتولى الله ويلتجيء إليه كل محتاج مضطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading is God's victory for believers and vengeance against their foes, vindicating the believer's hope that God would replace his lost garden.
rows.anchor: ينصر بها أولياءه المؤمنين على الكفرة وينتقم لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ‘there’ points to the Hereafter, where God alone has sovereignty and gives believers the best reward and final outcome.
rows.anchor: أن قوله هنالك إشارة إلى الدار الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUqban, ʿuqbā, and the cited variants all mean the final outcome.
rows.anchor: وكلها بمعنى العاقبة

none: Qur'an text only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining the world's lowliness and the Resurrection's honor, al-Razi presents the scene as a response to pagans boasting of wealth and supporters over poor Muslims.
rows.anchor: لما بين خساسة الدنيا وشرف القيامة أردفه بأحوال القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day clause may mean ‘remember the day’ and attach to the command to give the parable; alternatives make the events occur that day or qualify ‘better hope.’ The first reading is clearest.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنه يكون التقدير واذكر لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read the mountains as the subject of passive tusayyar; others read active nusayyiru with mountains as object. The meaning is the same because God moves them; al-Kashshaf transmits another reading.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر تسير على فعل ما لم يسم فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though the destination is not stated, al-Razi says the correct meaning is that God makes the mountains cease to exist, as shown by verses about their pulverization and the level plain.
rows.anchor: والحق أن المراد أنه تعالى يسيرها إلى العدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that buildings, mountains, and trees disappear, leaving the earth uncovered and level.
rows.anchor: لم يبق على وجهها شيء من العمارات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the earth exposes its interior by casting out its buried dead.
rows.anchor: أنها أبرزت ما في بطنها وقذفت الموتى المقبورين فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation is that regions become visible after God removes the mountains and seas that concealed them.
rows.anchor: وجوه الأرض كانت مستورة بالجبال والبحار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gathers every person, first and last, for judgment and leaves no one out.
rows.anchor: جمعناهم للحساب فلم نغادر منهم أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yughadir means leave behind; related examples are betrayal as leaving a pledge, a pool left by floodwater, and a braid left behind.
rows.anchor: ومعنى لم نغادر لم نترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of ‘in a row’ has everyone in one visible row with none screening another; al-Qaffal relates saff to exposure like a level plain.
rows.anchor: تعرض الخلق كلهم على الله صفا واحدا ظاهرين بحيث لا يحجب بعضهم بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, people may stand in successive rows, as around the Kaaba; singular saff can mean rows, as tiflan can mean children.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد أن يكون الخلق صفوفا يقف بعضهم وراء بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation is that they stand upright, like the ṣawāff of sacrificial camels.
rows.anchor: صفا أي قياما ، كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: المشبهة
rows.claim: The anthropomorphists argue that God's coming with the angels and people being presented to Him places God physically at the gathering.
rows.anchor: قالت المشبهة قوله تعالى : { وجاء ربك والملك صفا صفا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Presentation means people stand where God questions and judges them, not that God occupies a place or comes to see them after not seeing them.
rows.anchor: لا على أنه تعالى يحضر في مكان وعرضوا عليه ليراهم بعد أن لم يكن يراهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being brought back as first created does not mean equality in every respect: people were once small, irrational, and unaccountable; now they appear barefoot, naked, without wealth or support.
rows.anchor: لأنهم خلقوا صغارا ولا عقل لهم ولا تكليف عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address recalls that pagans denied resurrection while boasting of wealth and supporters; now they have left those assets behind and witnessed the truth of resurrection.
rows.anchor: كنتم مع التعزز على المؤمنين بالأموال والأنصار تنكرون البعث والقيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person's record is placed in the right or left hand; ‘the Book’ generically means the records of deeds.
rows.anchor: يوضع في هذا اليوم كتاب كل إنسان في يده إما في اليمين أو في الشمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Criminals fear both punishment for their evil deeds and exposure before the gathered people.
rows.anchor: خائفين مما في الكتاب من أعمالهم الخبيثة وخائفين من ظهور ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No sin, minor or major, is omitted; ihsa means recording and containing everything, and the feminine forms assume ‘deed.’
rows.anchor: لا يترك شيئا من المعاصي سواء كانت أو كبيرة إلا وهي مذكورة في هذا الكتاب

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars say people cry over minor sins before major ones because the minor sins led them into the greater sins.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العلماء : ضجوا من الصغائر قبل الكبائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deeds are found present either in the pages themselves or as their recompense.
rows.anchor: في الصحف عتيدا أو جزاء ما عملوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wrongs no one: He records no uncommitted act, does not increase deserved punishment, and does not punish one person for another's offense.
rows.anchor: معناه أنه لا يكتب عليه ما لم يفعل

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i argues that punishing people for acts they did not commit would be unjust.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي : هذه الآية تدل على فساد قول المجبرة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: He also says the verse rules out punishing children without sin and rules out punishing without offense merely because creation belongs to God.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يعذب الأطفال بغير ذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi answers the first claims by counterargument from knowledge and motive; the third fails because saying God should not take a son does not imply that taking a son is possible.
rows.anchor: أما الجواب عن الأولين فهو المعارضة بالعلم والداعي

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says three people are questioned on Judgment Day: a slave, a sick person, and a ruler; each excuse is challenged by comparison with Yusuf, Ayyub, or Sulayman, who served despite similar or greater burdens.
rows.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( يحاسب الناس في القيامة

rows.speaker: معاذ عن رسول الله
rows.claim: Muadh reports that the Prophet said a servant is asked about body, lifespan, wealth's source and spending, and knowledge put into practice.
rows.anchor: وعن معاذ عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( لن يزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims agree sins include minor and major, but the Mu'tazila define major by punishment exceeding the agent's reward and minor by punishment falling below it.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : الكبيرة ما يزيد عقابه على ثواب فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi rejects that definition because it assumes deeds intrinsically generate reward and punishment, an idea he refuted in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: أن هذا الحد إنما يصح لو ثبت أن الفعل يوجب ثوابا وعقابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He instead measures sin by ignorance of God and harm to others; the corresponding virtues are reverence for God and compassion for creation.
rows.anchor: الطاعات محصورة في نوعين : التعظيم لأمر الله والشفقة على خلق الله

none: Qur'an text only; no commentary in this segment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of Iblis mirrors pagans' pride toward poor Muslims: Iblis exalted fiery ancestry over Adam's clay, as the pagans invoked noble lineage and wealth; the warning rejects that conduct.
rows.anchor: إبليس إنما تكبر على آدم لأنه افتخر بأصله ونسبه

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi offers another coherence link: after the Resurrection and the record, the text asks idolaters where their partners are; since Iblis leads to shirk, his story is introduced first, and repetition gives each passage a new benefit.
rows.anchor: وكان قد علم تعالى أن إبليس هو الذي يحمل الإنسان على إثبات هؤلاء الشركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One position says Iblis was an angel, compatible with the word jinn through an angelic tribe called jinn, shared hiddenness, or association with Paradise; Sa'id ibn Jubayr reportedly calls him an angelic gardener.
rows.anchor: أنه من الملائكة وكونه من الملائكة لا ينافي كونه من الجن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second position makes Iblis the father of the jinn devils, who were created from fire.
rows.anchor: أنه من الجن الذين هم الشياطين والذين خلقوا من نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third position says Iblis was an angel who was transformed.
rows.anchor: قول من قال كان من الملائكة فمسخ وغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi's argument against Iblis being an angel is that he has descendants, while angels have no offspring; other objections are answered elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أصل ما يدل على أنه ليس من الملائكة أنه تعالى أثبت له ذرية ونسلا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains fasqa as leaving obedience, like a date leaving its husk or a mouse leaving its hole.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : ففسق عن أمر ربه أي خرج عن طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi cites Ru'ba's rajaz line about transgressors straying from their intended course to illustrate the root sense of departure.
rows.anchor: يهوين في نجد وغور غائرا … فواسقا عن قصدها جوائرا

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh, as quoted by al-Zajjaj, say the command caused Iblis's disobedience; without it the rebellion would not have occurred.
rows.anchor: حكى الزجاج عن الخليل وسيبويه أنه قال : لما أمر فعصى

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub takes the phrase to mean Iblis rejected his Lord's command, with an omitted verb as in ‘ask the town’ or ‘ask the caravan.’
rows.anchor: قال قطرب : فسق عن أمر ربه رده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pagans' social arrogance copies Iblis, so the verse asks how they could follow one whom they know to be their enemy.
rows.anchor: إنكم في هذا القول اقتديتم بإبليس في تكبره على آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke seems to rely on belief in Iblis's existence, progeny, enmity, and the pagans' imitation, all of which depend on Muhammad's report.
rows.anchor: كل هذه المقدمات الأربعة لا سبيل إلى إثباتها إلا بقول النبي محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi answers that pagans had heard the story from People of Scripture and believed it, so the comparison could deter their pride.
rows.anchor: المشركين كانوا قد سمعوا قصة إبليس وآدم من أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i argues that God neither wills nor creates unbelief: if He created and punished it, God's harm would exceed Iblis's, making the rebuke incoherent.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي في هذه الآية دلالة على أنه تعالى لا يريد الكفر ولا يخلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi answers the argument from divine will and creation by counterargument from motive and knowledge.
rows.anchor: والجواب : المعارضة بالداعي والعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pagans rejected Muhammad from arrogance; anyone acting or speaking to boast, including displaying knowledge or debating to elevate himself, imitates Iblis.
rows.anchor: فهذا يدل على أن كل من أقدم على عمل أو قول بناء على هذا الداعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis is a bad substitute for God for whoever replaces obedience to God with obedience to him.
rows.anchor: أي بئس البدل من الله إبليس لمن استبدله به فأطاعه

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: The majority take the pronoun in ‘I did not make them witness’ as the beings people adopted as allies; God did not enlist them to witness creation or rely on them, and ‘misleaders’ explains who they are.
rows.anchor: أن المعنى ما أشهدت الذي اتخذتموهم أولياء خلق السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi prefers that the pronoun refer to disbelievers who demanded that poor Muslims be expelled: they were not partners in governing the world, and the nearest antecedent supports this reading.
rows.anchor: وهو أقرب عندي أن الضمير عائد إلى الكفار الذين قالوا للرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation is that unbelievers were not shown the primordial decree of happiness and misery, so they cannot claim superiority when their worldly and final ranks may reverse.
rows.anchor: كون هؤلاء الكفار جاهلين بما جرى به القلم في الأزل

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf reads the conjunction in ‘I was not’ with fatḥa, addressing Muhammad: it was not fitting for him to rely on or take pride in them.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) قرىء وما كنت بالفتح

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reads muttakhidh al-mudillīn with nunation, retaining the original form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي رضوان الله عليه : { متخذ المضلين } بالتنوين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads ʿuḍdan with a still dād and shifts its vowel to ʿayn; further variants include two dammas or two fatḥas, and the word means helper or supporter.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : { عضدا } بسكون الضاد ونقل ضمتها إلى العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage returns to Judgment Day after explaining that the pagans' boasting imitates Iblis.
rows.anchor: لما قرر أن القول الذي قالوه في الافتخار على الفقراء اقتداء بإبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza reads first-person plural ‘We say,’ linked to God's earlier ‘We said to the angels’; the other readers use third-person ‘he says.’
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة : ( نقول ) بالنون عطفا على قوله : { وإذ قلنا للملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause can mean ‘remember the day We say,’ linked to the earlier command to the angels.
rows.anchor: واذكر يوم نقول عطفا على قوله : { وإذ قلنا للملائكة اسجدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is told to make idolaters call their alleged partners, meaning the jinn they worshiped, for aid and intercession; they receive no answer or benefit. Another verse gives their words to the partners.
rows.anchor: أي ادعوا من زعمتم أنهم شركاء لي حيث أهلتموهم للعبادة

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf defines mawbiq as destruction or a place of annihilation; one account places a ravine in Hell between pagans and the angels or Jesus they worshiped.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : الموبق المهلك من وبق يبق

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets mawbiq as enmity so intense that it is ruinous, supporting it with a poem about love and hatred.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : ( موبقا ) أي عداوة والمعنى عداوة هي في شدتها هلاك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains the word as their connection or bond, which becomes their ruin on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء البين المواصلة أي جعلنا مواصلتهم في الدنيا هلاكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is a distant barrier between unbelievers in Hell's depths and the angels or Jesus in the highest gardens, so remote that a traveler perishes crossing it.
rows.anchor: الموبق البرزخ البعيد أي جعلنا بين هؤلاء الكفار وبين الملائكة وعيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unbelievers' ‘thought’ may mean certain knowledge that they will enter the Fire.
rows.anchor: أن الظن ههنا بمعنى العلم واليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More plausibly, they see the Fire from afar and expect immediate entry without reprieve because of its fury and roar.
rows.anchor: وهو الأقرب أن المعنى أن هؤلاء الكفار يرون النار من مكان بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muwāqiʿūhā means entering or mingling with the Fire; intense mixing is called muwāqaʿah.
rows.anchor: أي مخالطوها فإن مخالطة الشيء لغيره إذا كانت قوية تامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They find no diversion from it because the angels drive them toward it.
rows.anchor: أي لم يجدوا عن النار معدلا إلى غيرها لأن الملائكة تسوقهم إليها

none: Qur'an text only; no commentary in this segment.
